chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah, from his forefathers (peace be upon them), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever desires that goodness be abundant in his house, let him perform ablution (wudu) when his food is presented.'
ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of performing ablution before eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this tradition from Imam Ali (peace be upon him), linking the physical purity of *wudu* with the spiritual and material abundance of the home. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating ritual cleanliness into daily domestic routines to invite divine blessings (*barakah*) and maintain a state of readiness for worship.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-44 Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his uncle Muhammad ibn Abil-Qasim quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Al-Qasim ibn Yahya, on the authority of his grandfather Al-Hassan ibn Rashid, on the authority of Abi Basir, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB) that the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) said, “Whoever wants to have an increase in goodness in his house should make ablutions before eating.”
